issues.issue: The review note says no breakdown is printed, but the Statement of Activities (p2) has one: Charges for Services 560,651 + Interest income 711,090 + Miscellaneous 1,320,567 = 2,592,308 exactly. The Taxes line was split using the same page. As recorded, 711,090 of investment income and 560,651 of charges are hidden in other. Miscellaneous is only about 51% of the line.
Broad group. It includes sale of surplus 29,154 (p7), which the governmental funds statement treats as other financing, so that asset sale is counted as revenue in detail.
The category rules list noxious weed control under natural resources/conservation. The report prints it under the Public Works heading, so the choice is defensible.
Single line. Per p5 the Road disbursements are public works 2,944,295 + capital outlay 6,007,348 + bond issuance costs 176,250, so about two-thirds is capital outlay and part is debt service.
No function is printed. The actual is 0, so there is no effect on amounts.

The fund columns (pp8-9) show 911 Emergency 15,753, Health Department 23,448 (matches the Public assistance charges for services on p2), Preservation & Modernization 4,940 and STOP 640. These are mostly fees and charges, so charges for services/fees looks like the better fit than other.
No object is printed. It comes from Miscellaneous Sinking 56,994, 911 Wireless 14,500 and 911 Emergency 3,649, which may be equipment. The construction/infrastructure category is a guess.

The amounts are correct as printed on the combining schedule. However, the detail transfers then total 5,426,951 in and 5,426,951 out, against 5,416,813 on the governmental funds statement (p6). The 10,138 difference is the 911 Holding transfer between nonmajor funds, which p6 eliminates. The same applies to detail[53] (-23,707 vs -13,569 on p6).

Both schedules add up internally. The 4,240 (and the General Fund 29,154) is sale of surplus that one schedule puts in Local and the other in other financing. This is a classification difference, not a report that fails to add up.
